messages:
Cleo (CS): Heads up — customer acme-retail just opened an escalation: model responses changed after last rollout. They say previously correct policy answers are now hallucinating small policy names. Internal evals on our benchmark passed. Can we repro?

Ahmed (SE): Thanks. Do we have example prompt + before/after outputs and request ids? Also which deployment/model variant?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: model:redwood-instruct@v1.4.0 -> canary 25% at 2026-03-10T04:21:00Z (triggered by release pipeline) :rocket:

Cleo (CS): Pasted what customer sent: they provided one prompt and two outputs (old vs new).
```
PROMPT: "List the compliance steps for handling POS transaction disputes in EU regions. Keep step names short."
OLD_OUTPUT (v1.3.2): "1) Verify transaction. 2) Log dispute. 3) Escalate to Payments Ops."
NEW_OUTPUT (v1.4.0): "1) Verify transaction. 2) Log dispute. 3) Escalate to PhantomOps (refer to internal doc)."
REQUEST_ID: req_20260310_42
```

Linh (ML Eng): Hmm. That 'PhantomOps' smells like a tokenization / embedding mismatch or a system-prompt change that favors internal aliases. Our evals probably didn't include these exact short, constrained prompts. Can we run a replay with the customer's raw prompt + context?

Ahmed (SE): Running a quick local compare with the same seed and deterministic decode: gave different outputs depending on temperature and system prompt. On hosted we use temperature=0.0 for policy endpoints — is customer calling through our 'chat' route with default temp?

Cleo (CS): Customer said they call /v1/generate with no temperature param (defaults to 1). They used an older SDK version though. They also included a small system instruction: "You are a compliance assistant."

Linh (ML Eng): Two hypotheses: (1) decoding randomness (temp) + new weights led to aliasing on short names; (2) model alias table / tokenizer update introduced subword that maps to 'PhantomOps' bias. Quick tests: run canonical internal benchmark (we already did) + run a 'customer prompt slice' test set (the set of real customer prompts) — if failure appears only on customer slice, we have an eval gap.

Jordan (PM): Can we get a reproducible test harness that replays the exact HTTP request headers and SDK version? Also, request_id from customer would let infra pull logs.

Ahmed (SE): I pulled logs for req_20260310_42:
```
{ "request_id": "req_20260310_42", "model": "redwood-instruct@v1.4.0", "temperature": 1, "route": "chat", "sdk_version": "node-0.9.1" }
```
Trace shows response streamed in three chunks; chunk 3 contained the hallucinated alias. No error codes. Latency normal.

Linh (ML Eng): Replayed locally with the same headers, temp=1, seed unknown (non-deterministic): got PhantomOps in 1/20 runs. With temp=0 -> output matches v1.3.2. That suggests decoding/determinism is major factor. But why only after v1.4.0? Possibly small probability mass shift created by fine-tune/merge.

Cleo (CS): Customer insists behavior changed deterministically for them (they always see the alias). They use node-0.9.1; could SDK include different prompt construction? Maybe it appends a hidden system message?

Ahmed (SE): Good catch — SDK 0.9.1 had a bug where it appended a short context hint for telemetry: "note: see internal ops" as a system message (we patched in 0.9.2). If that hidden hint was present, it could bias outputs toward internal names.

Jordan (PM): Action list: 1) Confirm SDK bug presence in that customer's calls (Cleo), 2) Run customer-prompt-slice tests against v1.3.2 and v1.4.0 with temp=1 and with temp=0 and with/without the hidden hint, 3) If repro is deterministic for them, consider rolling back canary or altering canary weights, 4) Notify customer about SDK upgrade and suggest temp=0 for deterministic responses.

Linh (ML Eng): I'll run the slice tests now. Quick results: out of 120 customer prompts, v1.3.2 + no-hint + temp=0 had 2 failures; v1.4.0 + no-hint + temp=0 had 3 failures (comparable). v1.4.0 + hint + temp=1 had 18 failures and many hallucinated short aliases. So the SDK-hidden-hint + higher temp amplifies the regression.

Cleo (CS): Customer is on SDK 0.9.1 and says they didn't set temperature -> defaults to 1. So likely root cause is SDK bug combined with v1.4.0's tiny distribution shift.

Ahmed (SE): Recommendation: reach out to customer with immediate mitigation steps: upgrade SDK to 0.9.2 (removes hint) or set temperature=0 for stricter answers. Meanwhile reduce canary weight to 0% for redwood-instruct@v1.4.0 until we confirm.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback: model:redwood-instruct@v1.4.0 -> canary 0% at 2026-03-10T06:10:00Z (initiated by Ahmed) :white_check_mark:

Jordan (PM): We'll also add this customer's prompt to the customer-prompt-slice used in evals to close the gap. Linh, please file a short postmortem item so we can add SDK-version matrix to regression tests.

Linh (ML Eng): Filing follow-ups: add SDK-version telemetry to eval harness, add 'hidden-hint' adversarial tests, and increase weight on short constrained prompts.

Cleo (CS): Sent customer a note: "We found interaction between SDK 0.9.1 hidden hint + model v1.4.0 + default temperature=1. We've rolled back canary and recommend upgrading SDK or passing temperature=0. We'll follow up with a patch and longer-term fixes." :raised_hands:

Ahmed (SE): Closing loop — please paste any additional customer logs if they show deterministic output after upgrading the SDK.

Cleo (CS): Will do. Thanks team!
